evidence.source_title: BEA API for Data Retrieval User Guide (April 20, 2026)
evidence.summary: "users must obtain a unique 36-character UserID by registering"; UserID is a minimum parameter on every request. Registration required; disposable e-mail addresses rejected.

evidence.source_title: BEA API User Guide - API Calling Limits
evidence.summary: Three standard limits for all accounts: 100 requests per minute, 100 MB data volume per minute, 30 errors per minute; exceeding any triggers a timeout period of about one minute.
The user guide section reviewed does not document exposure of originally-published vintages versus currently-revised values.
No official BEA market-consensus product was found; expectations would require a separate provider.
GDP Advance / Second / Third Estimate appear as separately scheduled, separately titled release events - naturally representable as append-only distinct events rather than mutations of one value.
Static JSON/XML API responses; byte-for-byte preservation straightforward.
An "Archive" section for past news releases is linked; the depth and per-document permanence were not verified in this pass.
Times such as "8:30 AM" and "10:00 AM" are listed, but NO timezone is stated on the schedule page.

evidence.source_title: BEA API User Guide - Data Return Format
evidence.summary: JSON or XML via the ResultFormat parameter; JSON is the default.
v1.0 is unregistered/keyless; v2.0 "Registration is required" and returns a key by email. Credential friction applies only to v2.0.
v2.0: 500 daily queries, 50 series/query, 20 years/query. v1.0: 25 daily queries, 25 series/query, 10 years/query.
No documentation found on whether the API exposes originally-published vintages or only the current (possibly revised) series. This is the central causal question for macro values.
The FAQ does not document any per-value publication timestamp or release date. Absence of documentation only - NOT evidence it is unsupported.

No official BLS market-consensus product was found. BLS publishes official statistics; market expectations would require a separate, independent provider. Recorded as UNKNOWN rather than NOT_SUPPORTED because absence of evidence is not proof of absence.
Releases carry a USDL identifier (e.g. USDL-26-1191), an agency-assigned document number usable as a deterministic identity component.

evidence.source_title: CPI News Release (news.release/cpi.htm and archived PDFs)
evidence.summary: News release documents carry "Transmission of material in this release is embargoed until 8:30 a.m. (ET)" - explicit time WITH timezone on the primary document, unlike the schedule page.
No documented field or footnote code distinguishing preliminary from revised values was found in the FAQ.
Static HTML and PDF release documents; byte-for-byte preservation straightforward.
Dated archive URLs of the form /news.release/archives/cpi_08122025.pdf preserve each release as originally published, which is the surface that can reconstruct original (unrevised) values.
Schedule lists "Release Time: 08:30 AM" per reference month, but NO timezone is stated on the schedule page itself.
Public pages and feeds; no authentication encountered or documented as required.
The FOMC calendar page does NOT state release times; the exact time lives on each statement document, not the schedule.

Documents follow a date-based pattern monetary{YYYYMMDD}{a|b}{n} (page and PDF). Stable and parseable, but it is a URL/date convention rather than an agency-assigned opaque identifier like an accession number.
The statement page and its PDF carry "For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT" - minute precision WITH an explicit timezone, on the primary document.
The feeds page documents no update frequency and no timestamp semantics for feed items. Item-level pubDate semantics were not officially confirmed.
Materials linked from this page span 2021-2027. Deeper historical archives exist elsewhere on the site but their release-time metadata was not verified in this pass.
Official RSS/XML feeds published, including /feeds/press_all.xml and /feeds/press_monetary.xml (monetary policy press releases).
"The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision."
A separate "Last Update: June 17, 2026" field exists, date-only. Per design section 7 this is site-maintenance metadata and must NOT be treated as publication time.
No official documentation found stating whether released statements can be corrected in place or how corrections would be exposed.
acceptanceDateTime is present on filings.recent and follows ISO-8601 of shape YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ. Observed uniformly across a 400-value sample of one company's filings; no sample rows retained.
Millisecond field representation (.sss). Supersedes the earlier UNKNOWN, which was an environment limitation rather than a documentation gap.

evidence.source_title: SEC Financial Statement and Notes Data Sets - SUB field definitions
evidence.summary: The corresponding documented field is defined as: "The ACCEPTANCE date and time of the registrant's filing with the Commission. Filings accepted after 5:30pm EST are considered filed on the following business day." The field therefore marks ACCEPTANCE by the Commission, not public dissemination.
Values carry a trailing Z (UTC) in every sampled value.

evidence.source_title: Determine the Status of My Filing
evidence.summary: Acceptance is NOT proven equivalent to dissemination. Submissions transmitted after 5:30 p.m. ET "will not be disseminated by EDGAR until the next business day", so acceptance can precede public availability by hours. Using acceptanceDateTime as source_available_at would create lookahead for those filings.

No official machine-readable field linking an amendment to the filing it amends was verified. Amendment FORM TYPES (10-K/A etc.) are distinguishable, and each submission carries its own accession number, but an explicit parent pointer was not established. prevrpt is not such a pointer.

Amendment form types (10-K/A, 10-Q/A, 8-K/A) exist and each submission receives its own accession number, implying append-only filing lineage rather than in-place mutation. The exact linkage field between an amendment and its original was not confirmed officially.

The documented "typical processing delay of less than a second" describes surface UPDATE latency relative to SEC dissemination. It is guidance, not a service-level guarantee, and it is not a publication timestamp.
"These APIs do not require any authentication or API keys to access." No credential friction.
companyfacts.zip and submissions.zip offered under /Archives/edgar/daily-index/, "recompiled nightly".
Accession number is a unique identifier assigned automatically by EDGAR to an accepted submission; format ##########-YY-SSSSSS (CIK, 2-digit year, 6-digit sequence). Not URL-derived.

"The submissions API is updated with a typical processing delay of less than a second; the xbrl APIs ... under a minute." JSON "updated throughout the day, in real time, as submissions are disseminated."
"Our current maximum access rate is 10 requests per second", "carefully monitored to preserve equitable access for all users."

evidence.source_title: SEC Financial Statement and Notes Data Sets
evidence.summary: filed/filingDate is "The date of the registrant's filing with the Commission", a DATE (no time). Combined with the post-cutoff rule it is an ASSIGNED business date and can differ from the acceptance date. It is not an exact publication instant; at best it supports date-only conservative semantics.

evidence.source_title: Determine the Status of My Filing
evidence.summary: "Most live submissions that begin transmission after 5:30 p.m. ET ... will receive a filing date of 6:00 a.m. ET the next business day and will not be disseminated by EDGAR until the next business day." Forms 3/4/5/144 and MEF extended to 10:00 p.m. ET same-date dissemination. EDGAR hours 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. ET. filingDate is therefore an ASSIGNED BUSINESS DATE, not a publication instant.
Four JSON APIs named: submissions, companyconcept, companyfacts, frames, under data.sec.gov.

evidence.source_title: Determine the Status of My Filing
evidence.summary: "Most live submissions that begin transmission after 5:30 p.m. ET ... will receive a filing date of 6:00 a.m. ET the next business day and will not be disseminated by EDGAR until the next business day." Forms 3/4/5/144 and certain MEF types are extended to 10:00 p.m. ET same-date dissemination. The rule is form-conditional and is NOT generalised here beyond the quoted scope.

evidence.source_title: SEC Financial Statement and Notes Data Sets
evidence.summary: prevrpt: "Previous Report - TRUE indicates that the submission information was SUBSEQUENTLY AMENDED prior to the end cutoff date of the data set." Its value depends on events AFTER the filing and on the dataset cutoff, so it is future-aware and retrospective by construction. It is NOT an amendment parent pointer and MUST NOT enter a causal record or feature at the filing's historical timestamp.

No per-filing public-dissemination timestamp was verified on the Submissions surface. Its field inventory is acceptanceDateTime, accessionNumber, act, core_type, fileNumber, filingDate, filmNumber, form, isInlineXBRL, isXBRL, isXBRLNumeric, items, primaryDocDescription, primaryDocument, reportDate, size. This is a statement about the SELECTED surface only, not about all SEC systems.
Static JSON and filing documents served over HTTPS from /Archives/; byte-for-byte preservation is straightforward, no JS rendering required.

Filings are third-party submissions and may embed filer-owned or third-party copyrighted material (exhibits, logos, images). No official statement establishing redistribution rights for filer-submitted content was verified. SEC-produced API metadata, filer content, HyprL normalized metadata and derived aggregates must be treated as distinct rights categories; no blanket public-domain assumption is made.
No explicit redistribution/licence statement was verified in this pass. US federal agency material is commonly public domain, but that was NOT confirmed from an official terms page.
Declared User-Agent required, documented format: "Sample Company Name AdminContact@<sample company domain>.com".

note: Provider property verification against the frozen causal design, revision 2. Corrects a materially overstated SEC timestamp claim found by independent counter-review: acceptanceDateTime is precise but marks acceptance, not public dissemination. No capture spec is frozen and no provider code exists. Absence of official documentation is recorded as UNKNOWN, never as false.

safe_live_policy.no_derived_0600_timestamp: a conservative next-business-day 06:00 ET bound is NOT adopted; its exact domain is not established and V1 does not invent it
safe_live_policy.observed_at: the collector's first successful acquisition of the public resource
safe_live_policy.source_available_at: null / unavailable - never derived from acceptance or filingDate
safe_live_policy.why_this_is_safe: a collector cannot observe a filing before EDGAR disseminates it, so observed_at naturally prevents lookahead. DURABLE_OBSERVED then gates on max(observed_at, ingested_at), which the design explicitly supports when source_available_at is absent.

sec_edgar.timestamp_caution: THREE separate cautions. (1) filingDate is an ASSIGNED business date, not an exact publication instant. (2) acceptanceDateTime is precise (ISO-8601, UTC, ms) but marks ACCEPTANCE, and is NOT proven equivalent to public dissemination; for post-cutoff filings acceptance precedes dissemination by hours. (3) source_available_at must therefore NOT be populated from either field as an exact dissemination instant. When no dissemination timestamp is available, the safe causal boundary is the collector's observed_at.

recommendation.confidence_change_reason: lowered from MEDIUM_HIGH: the earlier recommendation partly rested on a timestamp claim that did not survive independent review
recommendation.consensus_gap: No official market-consensus product was found at any of the four agencies. Consensus will require a separate, independently verified provider. This does NOT block 6G-A, whose objective is ingestion and replay, not surprise.

not_first.bea: registration required, no verified release identity, and no timezone on the schedule page
not_first.bls: richest macro relevance but the API's vintage and revision semantics are undocumented, and the schedule page omits a timezone; the causal surface is the dated release archive, which is a heavier first integration

recommendation.selection_reason: SEC still wins, but explicitly NOT on its source timestamp - it has none that is verified. It wins on the infrastructure axes 6G-A actually has to prove: an agency-ASSIGNED deterministic identity (accession number) rather than a URL convention; append-only submissions where each accession is an independent immutable observation; a documented access contract (10 req/s, declared User-Agent); no credentials; nightly bulk archives for deterministic offline fixtures; and enough event volume to exercise the store. There is also a positive reason its timestamp weakness helps: with no dissemination instant, SEC forces 6G-A to exercise the source_available_at = null path with observed_at bounding - a path design rev4 explicitly supports and which MUST be proven to work. A provider with a perfect source timestamp would leave that path untested.
recommendation.why_not_fed_despite_better_timestamp: The Fed has the better timestamp by a clear margin and is the right SECOND provider precisely because it exercises the source-declared-instant path. It loses first place on identity (date-based URL convention, not an agency-assigned id), on UNKNOWN revision and correction semantics, on an UNKNOWN rate/fair-access policy, and on event volume: roughly eight FOMC decisions a year is thin for shaking out an EventStore.
